answer: To thwart Sybil multiplication, dynamic opportunity-cost bonds mandate asymmetric staking collateral, whereby adversarial actions crossing a zero-knowledge verifiable delay trigger slashing penalties. Forging one quill into numerous identities requires immense capital barriers, rendering the marginal pearl of illicit gain inadequate to recover the expropriated copper collateral. Thus, expected attack utility remains strictly negative under this subgame-perfect punishment matrix, converging rational agents to a robust Nash equilibrium where honest participation is optimal.
